channel.title: Donetsk 2011 · updates
channel.description: Every change to the Donetsk 2011 game, site and research.

item.title: Site · v6.8 · Tram 1: rails and oncoming trams where they belong
item.description:
Fixed the track geometry in the cab view: no more doubled rails, the oncoming tram runs on the second track, and cars and pedestrians stay off the tram tracks.

New

  • Trees no longer stand on the rails: 372 removed from the tracks, 186 given smaller crowns so they do not overhang the line
  • Our own track is drawn only from the route line; duplicate OSM tracks within 2.4 m are removed
  • The second track is measured from OSM every 4 m; the oncoming tram follows it exactly and does not appear where there is no second track
  • The oncoming tram now faces us, headlights first
  • Cars on one-way carriageways drive only in the permitted direction, centred in their half
  • Cars and pedestrians never appear within 2.6–2.7 m of the rails
  • Catenary poles only stand on free ground: not on the carriageway, the second track or inside buildings; a long bracket spans both tracks, and on wide streets a cross-span wire runs between poles on both sides (before: 126 of 330 poles stood on the road)
  • Street lamps move away from rails, roads and walls; where there is no room there is no lamp (before: about 300 of 3091 stood on tracks, roads or in buildings)
  • Stops: a platform only where the ground on the right is free; on streets people wait on the pavement past the kerb, not on a platform in the middle of the road
  • Where the track runs in the carriageway and at level crossings it lies in concrete slabs instead of ballast
  • Trees: 318 trunks inside buildings and 120 on carriageways removed; crowns next to walls narrowed so they no longer pass through walls
  • Home: a fourth way in under “Start here” — the cab ride on tram route 1
  • Section descriptions no longer mention the Zarichna walk, which is gone from the site
  • Press kit: the site description now includes the tram ride, the October 2011 chronicle and the radio

item.title: Site · v6.7 · Tram No. 1: 2012 shop signs and passers-by
item.description:
The buildings along the route now carry the signs of shops, cafés, bars and banks, and people walk along the pavements.

New

  • 84 signs from OpenStreetMap as of 13 September 2012: McDonald's, Velyka Kyshenia, the Yuzovka brewery pub, Chicago, the main post office, the Planeta mall and more
  • Where a place had no name in 2012, it carries a plain sign for its kind: Pharmacy, Groceries, Flowers
  • The signs light up at night
  • Passers-by walk along the pavements of the main streets
  • The ride is slower: twice real time by default, and you can ride in real time too (the ×1, ×2, ×5, ×15 button)

item.title: Site · v6.6 · Tram No. 1: the view from the cab
item.description:
The ride now shows the city from the driver’s seat: houses, streets, trees, poles and the overhead wire along all 11 kilometres of the route.

New

  • A 3D cab view from OpenStreetMap data along the whole line: 3,300 buildings, streets with markings and pavements, parks and water
  • Rails, the contact wire and its poles, platforms and shelters at the stops
  • A dashboard: speedometer, controller, door, run and brake lamps
  • Relief from SRTM data: the climbs and descents along the way
  • October trees along the streets and in the yards, cars on the streets, trams passing the other way
  • Street lamps, loggias on the five- and nine-storey blocks, people waiting at the stops
  • Time of day: now in Donetsk, day, evening or night; at night the windows, street lamps and headlights are lit
  • When a 2008–2013 photo was taken nearby, a button lets you look at it
  • The streets come from the current map; buildings put up in 2012 or later are removed

item.title: Site · v6.5 · Tram No. 1 now runs on the real track
item.description:
The ride on route 1 is rebuilt: the tram follows the route’s rails from OpenStreetMap, speeds up, slows for the curves and waits at the stops. The “Then and later” section is gone.

New

  • The path is the real route 1 line, 11.2 km, instead of straight lines between the stops
  • A destination board, speed, distance covered and travel time (an estimate, not a timetable)
  • A route diagram like the one inside the car: all 26 stops, tap any of them
  • The window shows 2008–2013 photos taken next to the line; where there are none, a view from above on the map
  • You can ride four times faster
  • The “Then and later” section with photos from after 2014 is removed from the site and the atlas

item.title: Site · v6.4 · A new look for the “Do you remember where this is?” game, and a clearer home page
item.description:
The game now opens the City page: a dark stage with a stack of photos, a single Play button and the four modes as cards. The home page has a new “Start here” block.

New

  • The game modes are cards that say what to do, how many rounds there are and your record
  • Play starts a game straight away; Photo of the day shows the day number and your streak
  • At the end of a game, a strip of all eight photos shows which ones you got right
  • You can answer with the 1–4 keys and press Enter to go on
  • The game comes first on the City page; it used to sit below the photo archive
  • The home page has three ways in: the game, the 3D model of the district and the photo archive

item.title: Site · v6.3 · Roads and traffic: widths from lanes, surfaces, 700 cars, tail lights
item.description:
The roads of the reference map are reworked. Carriageway widths come from the number of lanes and surfaces come from OSM. Traffic is denser and behaves better at junctions.

New

  • Carriageway widths follow the OSM lane count rather than the road class. Each half of a dual carriageway is no longer drawn 14 m wide. Markings, pavements, lamps, shelters, signals and trolleybus wires follow this width
  • Surfaces from the OSM tag: dirt streets of the private sector, cobbles, concrete
  • Tram tracks laid in the carriageway are drawn without ballast, rails straight on the asphalt (19 stretches)
  • Up to 700 cars instead of 380, more of them on the main streets; at the morning rush hour the average speed is about 20 km/h
  • At a junction without signals a car holds it until it has passed, the others wait at the edge
  • Cars no longer jump between lanes when they pass a node; they turn smoothly
  • Red tail lights at night

item.title: Site · v6.2 · First storey counts from the 2011 panoramas; a lighter map for phones
item.description:
A pass over the Google Street View panoramas taken in October 2011 has begun. Storeys are counted by eye and written into the project; the images themselves never reach the site. The building card marks such a height as class B.

New

  • Four buildings have storey counts from the panoramas: Kobozieva 4; Horkoho 61 (seen from Cheliuskintsiv Street); Artema 63 and Artema 71
  • On phones and low-memory devices the map is built lighter: half the trees, no cars in the yards and no entrance details
  • 3D map audit: entrances now sit on the actual walls of the blocks rather than on their bounding box; trees, cars and wagons that ended up inside buildings or on roads are removed
  • The map takes about 140 MB of memory instead of almost 600 MB and opens faster
  • The Bis residential tower is removed: OSM dates its construction to 2012
  • Cars run into each other less often at junctions without signals
  • The river is no longer drawn as a strip across the reservoir; the spoil heap slope is no longer a flat stain
  • The evidence-mode legend now covers grade B; the traffic notes in the map card fold under "Traffic and map details"
  • October 2011 in colour: about a quarter of the crowns are already yellow and rust, almost half of the birches (illustrative)
  • People wait at the bus and tram stops, one to three by each shelter
  • The card of a building with storeys from a panorama now gives the storey count
  • A soft contact shadow at the foot of the larger buildings, so they no longer seem to hover over the ground

item.title: Site · v6.1 · The 3D opens on the reference map; markets, petrol stations, fountains, balconies
item.description:
The 3D model now opens straight on the whole 4.37 × 2.84 km reference map. The Zarechna Street quarter stays at its centre; to go back to the quarter alone, switch off the "Reference map" button. The map has more small things of the city, at the places OSM marks them.

New

  • About 190 market stalls with striped awnings at the Zhovtnevyi and Slovianskyi markets
  • About 340 cars in the open car parks
  • Pumps under the canopies of three petrol stations
  • Three fountains with a basin and a jet, the musical fountain among them
  • Swings, slides and sandboxes on the playgrounds, goals on the football pitches
  • Kiosks by about half of the bus stops
  • Balconies on the facades of the apartment blocks; pedestrians now walk instead of gliding
  • Entrances of the apartment blocks: a concrete canopy, a door, a bench and a lamp over the door that lights up in the evening (illustrative)
  • Shelters at the tram stops mapped in OSM 2012
  • Freight wagons — gondolas, tank cars, box cars — on the industrial spurs (illustrative)
  • Brick chimneys on the roofs of private houses, TV aerials on the roofs of the apartment blocks (illustrative)
  • The places come from OSM; the stalls, cars, swings and kiosks themselves are placed illustratively

item.title: Site · v6.0 · The 3D map comes alive: trolleybuses, pedestrians, power lines, street trees
item.description:
The reference map has more life and more city in it. Trolleybuses under their wires, pedestrians on the pavements, high-voltage lines, factory chimneys, trees along the main streets and cars in the yards are added. The map card says which of it rests on data and which is placed illustratively.

New

  • Trolleybus overhead wires over the streets of the routes: Artema, Leninskyi prospekt, Universytetska; trolleybuses with their poles run under them and stop at the stops
  • Pedestrians on the pavements of the main streets; at signalled junctions they cross at the zebras while the cars have red
  • 35 and 110 kV power lines from OSM: lattice towers and sagging wires
  • Factory chimneys with red and white bands, the water tower, the dark slope of the Tsentralno-Zavodska mine spoil heap
  • About 6,600 street trees: chestnuts and lindens, Lombardy poplars, birches (placement illustrative)
  • About 2,500 cars parked along the drives in the yards of the apartment blocks (illustrative)
  • Windows on large buildings with a known storey count, dark flat roofs, railings on the bridges

item.title: Site · v5.9 · A fuller reference map: fences, colours, storeys, yards
item.description:
The reference map is noticeably fuller. Everything OpenStreetMap already has but was not drawn before is now on it. Where there is no data, some gaps are filled with careful estimates, and each of them is labelled.

New

  • 771 fences and walls from OSM: private-sector plots, industrial sites, schools and hospitals are enclosed as the map shows
  • Wall and roof colours from OSM tags on 333 buildings: brick red, cream, grey
  • 211 large buildings without a storey count take their height from nearby buildings of the same shape whose storeys are known; the card marks this as an estimate
  • 38 sports pitches and playgrounds, 9 storage tanks
  • About 2,400 trees in the yards of private houses, on the side of the plot away from the street (illustrative)
  • 36 street names on the map instead of 16

item.title: Site · v5.8 · Lighter and more detailed 3D: pavements, stops, roofs
item.description:
The model is now half as heavy for the graphics card. The reference map draws only what is in view, and small details only up close. The headroom went into pavements, bus shelters and the roofs of the blocks of flats.

New

  • Normals, colours and facade coordinates are stored compactly: the geometry takes about half the memory
  • The map is split into 500 × 500 m tiles: tiles outside the view are skipped, and trees, lamps, markings and pavements are skipped beyond 1.1 km from the camera
  • Pavements with a kerb along the main streets; none on the medians of the avenues
  • Bus shelters at the 38 bus stops from OSM 2012
  • Parapets on the flat roofs of blocks of flats, and lift machine rooms on blocks of nine storeys and more
  • The pavements, shelters and roofs follow a typical layout, not photos of each building

item.title: Site · v5.7 · Streets of the reference map: markings, zebras, lamps and trees
item.description:
The streets of the reference map are more detailed now. The main roads have lane markings, the signals have stop lines and zebras, the avenues have lamps that come on in the evening, the parks and woods have trees, and the tram tracks have their overhead line.

New

  • A dashed centre line and lane dividers on the main streets; road joints at bends and junctions without gaps
  • Zebras and stop lines before every signal, plus 16 crossings where OSM had them in 2012
  • About 1,800 lamps along the main streets; after sunset they light up, and cars and trams have their headlights on
  • Trees in the woods and parks shown on the map, and poles with the contact wire over the tram tracks
  • The markings, lamps and trees follow a typical layout, not photos of each street

item.title: Site · v5.6 · The reference map comes alive: cars, trams and traffic lights
item.description:
The reference map now runs a small street-traffic simulation. Cars, minibuses, buses and trams drive its streets, stopping at red lights and at stops. The signals and stops stand where OpenStreetMap had them by September 2012, the earliest state of the map the OSM history keeps and the closest to 2011.

New

  • 29 signalled junctions with 87 signal heads: green, amber, red and an all-red pause between phases
  • 38 bus and 29 tram stops from OSM 2012; buses and trams wait at them for 11–18 seconds
  • Up to 380 cars, GAZelle minibuses, yellow buses and Tatra T3 trams; one-way streets and lane counts come from OSM
  • Traffic follows the hour on the sun slider: the streets are almost empty at night and busier in the rush hours
  • The cars, their routes and the signal timing are illustrative: a model, not a record of real traffic
  • A register of storey counts from 2011 Street View panoramas is ready; buildings checked against a panorama will get class B

item.title: Site · v5.5 · The next ring: the reference map in 3D
item.description:
The project grows in rings: a house, a corridor, the quarter, the reference map, the district, the city. The browser 3D model now opens the third ring. Around the Zarichna quarter rise 4.37 × 2.84 km of the city, with Artema and Postysheva streets, Komsomolskyi Avenue, the Kalmius and the city ponds.

New

  • 4,638 buildings on their OpenStreetMap outlines; 1,512 take their height from storeys or the height tag, the rest stand at a height typical for their type, marked as an estimate
  • Streets of every class, the railway and tram tracks, bridges, the Kalmius and Bakhmutka rivers, the Central and Second City Ponds, the Nyzhniokalmiuske reservoir, parks, woods and industrial zones
  • Only what is on the map: trees stand where OSM marks them, and buildings of unknown use get no invented windows
  • Tap any building on the map: type, height, where the height comes from, and a link to the object in OSM
  • The map loads only when you press “Reference map”, so the page itself stays light
  • SRTM relief for the whole map arrives with the next site update; until then the terrain outside the quarter is a placeholder

item.title: Site · v5.4 · 3D quarter: garages, substations and yards
item.description:
I checked the quarter’s models against the building types in OpenStreetMap. Until now everything that was not a house stood there as a house with a gable roof. Garages, substations, the canopy and outbuildings now look like what they are, and plots and yards have proper ground.

New

  • Garage rows are low, with flat roofs and a gate every 3.3 m, each gate a different colour
  • The 110 kV substation “Kalmiuska” is a two-storey brick hall with window bands and a gate; the transformer kiosk is a brick box with two steel doors and a yellow plate
  • The canopy over the drive stands on posts, not walls
  • House plots have a lawn in front, a vegetable garden behind and a paved path; the garage cooperative is asphalted; the blocks of flats have lawns and paths
  • The five-storey block at 38 Donetska no longer has a lift room on its roof: such blocks had no lifts. The roofs of both blocks get vent stacks and TV aerials
  • The building card shows the type and where it comes from, the OSM tags or a guess from the footprint and address, and the height the building is drawn at

item.title: Site · v5.3.1 · Time pips, to the standard
item.description: The radio’s time-signal station now plays the six pips before the news as they were: 1000 Hz, 0.1 s each, one a second, the start of the sixth being the exact time. They follow your clock, the sixth falling on :00 and :30, and sound the way they did from the kitchen speaker of the wired radio.

item.title: Site · v5.3 · Site audit: everything found is fixed
item.description:
The site went through a full check: 126 pages in four languages, on desktop and phone, in the light and dark themes. Everything it found is fixed.

New

  • The radio on the Sounds page now plays real field recordings: rain, a Prague tram, a stadium in Vienna, the RWM time station, night wind and trains. Each station credits its author and licence
  • The updates feed no longer floods the counter with requests when it is down or blocked
  • A link to /en/, /uk/ or /fi/ always opens in the language it was sent in
  • The language switch is made of real links, so it also works without JavaScript
  • Search: when nothing turns up in this language, it shows matches in the other three
  • Game screenshots load at screen size: on a phone the Press page is about 1.5 MB lighter
  • The radio dial stations and atlas pins are easier to tap, and the atlas card links are readable in the dark theme
  • In the Guests block you can turn off counting your visits; the site then sends nothing to country.is or Abacus
  • The postcard slides out of its envelope again when reduced motion is on

item.title: Site · v5.2 · Trams on Dzerzhinsky Avenue
item.description:
The 3D quarter now has the tram line that really runs here: two tracks on their own bed in the middle of Dzerzhinsky Avenue, sleepers and rails, low kerbs, centre poles with arms to both tracks and street lamps, and an overhead wire above each track. Tatra T3SU cars run on it: one cab, three doors on the right, a pantograph. In 2011 routes 9 and 10 of depot No. 3 ran here.

New

  • The line comes from OpenStreetMap and is aligned to the avenue's axis: in the OSM data it sits up to 3 m off the model's carriageways
  • The sources used show no stop inside the quarter, so the trams pass through without stopping
  • The cars wear the factory red-and-cream livery; the headway is shortened so a tram is more often in view
  • Cars on the avenue now keep to their side: the southern carriageway runs east, the northern one west

item.title: Site · v5.1 · A cleaner 3D quarter: no walk mode, no stray models
item.description:
The walk mode is gone completely. Models with no source behind them left the scene: playgrounds, garages, the bus stop and kiosk, washing, bushes, benches, mailboxes, dishes and cars in the yards. What stays is what the 2011 panoramas show and what is typical of these streets: plot fences, gates, the gas pipe, concrete poles with wires and street lamps. Trees were redrawn with round crowns, poplars along the avenues and a fruit tree in the yard of each private house.

New

  • The cars on the streets stay and are still illustrative
  • The model note was rewritten: what comes from sources and what is typical

item.title: Site · v5.0 · Fences by plot and traffic on the streets
item.description:
The fences of the 3D quarter were rebuilt from scratch. Every private house now has its own plot: a street fence with a gate and wicket, fences between neighbours and at the back. Corrugated sheet, picket fences, concrete sections with arches and lattice, brick gate pillars, a soil or gravel verge with a ragged asphalt edge and driveways to the gates. On Zarichna the gas pipe rises over every gate. Cars and a bus drive the streets: they keep their distance, give way at junctions and stop for the walker. Kerbs and pavements remain only on the avenues.

New

  • On Zarichna at houses 25–38 the fence type, gate colour, the gravel verge on the west side and the driveway surface come from the notes on the October 2011 panoramas
  • The other fences, the cars and their movement are illustrative
  • The cars carry no number plates

item.title: Site · v4.9 · Playgrounds in the yards of the apartment blocks
item.description:
The apartment blocks now have playgrounds with a sandpit, swings, a slide, a pull-up bar and a bench. Rubbish containers stand on a concrete pad by the end walls, and some balconies have satellite dishes. Cars look neater, with an underbody and wheels under the body.

New

  • Playgrounds, containers and dishes are illustrative: placed by the kind of place, not from photos

item.title: Site · v4.8 · Cars, garages and a bus stop in the 3D quarter
item.description:
Cars in the colours of the time stand along the yard driveways and now and then by the houses. Rows of metal garages with doors in different colours appeared next to the apartment blocks. The avenue has a bus shelter and a kiosk, and washing dries in the yards of private houses.

New

  • Cars, garages, the stop, the kiosk and the washing are illustrative: placed by the kind of place, not from photos
  • On the walk you can't pass through them

item.title: Site · v4.7 · Wires and benches on the streets of the 3D quarter
item.description:
Concrete poles with sagging wires now line the streets, with a wire running from them to every private house. Apartment entrances got benches, bushes grow in the yards and along the houses, gates have mailboxes, and the bigger roads have a centre line.

New

  • Poles, wires, benches, bushes and mailboxes are illustrative: placed by street type, not from photos
  • On the walk you can't pass through poles and benches

item.title: Site · v4.6 · Houses in 3D are now detailed
item.description:
Every house in the quarter got details: roof eaves, gable and hipped roofs, plinths, window sills, drainpipes, chimneys and doors with canopies. Apartment blocks now have balconies, entrance canopies and lift rooms on the roof.

New

  • On Zarichna at houses 25–38 wall and roof colours and roof shapes come from the research table built on the 2011 panoramas
  • Some private houses have TV aerials and satellite dishes, as in 2011
  • The other details are illustrative and picked by building type

item.title: Site · v4.5 · Fences, gates and a gas pipe in 3D
item.description:
The walk through the quarter is closer to the real street now: fences, gates with wickets, kerbs and a yellow gas pipe on posts line the houses.

New

  • At houses 25–38 on Zarichna the fence type comes from the notes on the October 2011 panoramas: corrugated sheet, picket, concrete panels, hedges
  • On the other streets fences are picked by house type and marked as illustrative
  • You can no longer walk through fences: you stay on the street, as in real life

Improved

  • The city, reconstruction and development pages are more compact: neighbouring blocks are grouped into tabs

item.title: Site · v4.3.1 · Site audit: speed, search and translations
item.description:
I checked all 36 pages in four languages: links, translations, accessibility, speed on a slow phone and what ends up in search. Everything found is fixed.

Improved

  • Pages come alive sooner on phones: headings are fitted without extra layout passes, the reveal animation no longer slows loading, and the header clock no longer keeps the processor busy
  • Every page has its own description for search engines and social media again, and the home page has a clear title
  • Weather chart labels and source names in the October chronicle are translated into every language
  • Site search closes on the first press of Esc, and the e-mail address no longer ends up in the search index
  • The caption over the 3D model and the step labels are readable in either theme; the “Guests” block names the services that count visits

item.title: Site · v4.3 · A walk down Zarichna, tram No. 1, a radio and postcards
item.description:
You can now walk through the 3D quarter yourself, at eye level. The city page lets you ride the whole tram No. 1 route, the sound page has an old receiver with “stations” to tune into, and you can send a friend a postcard from 2011.

New

  • First-person walk: keys or a joystick on phones, a sky with the sun and stars, autumn trees, the address of the house in your sights and a mini-map. Houses don’t let you walk through, windows and street lamps light up in the evening, birds sing by day and crickets at night
  • Panorama hunt: six spots where a Street View camera stood in October 2011 are marked with beams of light. The ones you find are remembered only on your device
  • Tram No. 1 from the railway station to the steelworks: 26 stops on the map, a stop display, the view from the window and sound made in the browser
  • Radio “Donetsk 2011”: a tuning knob, static between stations and six “stations” made of city sounds
  • A postcard from 2011: a photo, a stamp and a few handwritten lines; the envelope opens for the recipient, and the site stores nothing

Improved

  • Photos in the atlas can be sent as a postcard straight away
  • The Back and Next buttons of the guided walk on the reconstruction page have their labels back

item.title: Site · v4.2 · Evening in 3D, October 2011 day by day and place cards
item.description:
In the 3D quarter you can now wait for sunset: windows and street lamps light up. The city page has a chronicle of October 2011 with daily weather, matches and events. Every atlas place has its own card for social media, and the site itself got lighter.

New

  • The sun slider runs to 19:30: sunset at 17:41, dusk, lit windows and street lamps
  • “October 2011” chronicle: daily temperature and rain from the Donetsk weather station and 16 events of the month, each with its source
  • A “Share” button on atlas places: the link opens the place on the map and shows a photo card on social media
  • The atlas now shows 21 of the 22 archive photos

Improved

  • Fonts are almost half the size
  • Page header images in WebP with smaller copies for phones
  • Parts of a page below the screen are not drawn until you scroll to them, which is easier on phones

item.title: Site · v4.1 · Search, the site as an app and facades in 3D
item.description:
You can now search the site in all four languages. The site can be installed on a phone or computer, and pages you have read open without a connection. Houses in the 3D quarter now have colours and windows.

New

  • Search across pages, photos, “Then and later” and the update log: the magnifier button in the menu, the / key or Ctrl+K
  • Install the site as an app, with offline reading for pages you have opened and photos you have seen
  • Facades in the 3D quarter: windows, plinths and illustrative materials by building type, with a switch to turn them off
  • The atlas now shows 15 of the 22 archive photos and all four “Then and later” places

Improved

  • The house card names the illustrative facade material and says it is not taken from a photo
  • Archive photos open full size from the atlas

item.title: Site · v4.0 · Atlas, an address per language and faster photos
item.description:
Every photo on the site is now on one map of the city. Each language has its own address, so search engines find the site in all four languages. Photos are lighter and small text has more contrast.

New

  • An atlas on “The city” page: points for every photo and the “Then and later” places, photos on tap
  • Separate addresses /uk/, /en/, /fi/ with the text already in that language
  • A quiet hint when the page exists in your browser’s language
  • A “Skip to content” link for keyboard and screen reader users

Improved

  • Photos in WebP with smaller copies for phones: previews are about five times lighter
  • The script loads the texts of one language only
  • Small grey text has more contrast
  • Fonts are served from the site itself, not from Google

Fixed

  • The caption of the header photo no longer spills out of its frame
  • On narrow screens the home header text no longer runs off the edge

item.title: Site · v3.9 · Day and night on Donetsk time, “Then and later”, a sound diary
item.description:
The site now lives on Donetsk time: when it is night in Donetsk, the album goes dark. New: a “How to help” page, a sound diary and four places in the city before and after 2014.

New

  • A “now in Donetsk” clock in the menu and day and night that follow the sun over the city
  • “Then and later”: four places before and after 2014 with a time slider
  • A “How to help” page: photos, memories, the game, a link for friends
  • A “Sound diary”: a cassette player for future recordings and themes, made without AI

Improved

  • The theme button has three modes: Donetsk time, light and dark
  • Pages turn slightly warmer at dawn and dusk

item.title: Site · v3.8 · Site guests, RSS and a living album
item.description:
The site now has guests: you can see how many times people came here and from which countries. Updates can be followed via RSS, and the album pages came to life.

New

  • “Guests of Donetsk 2011” on the home page: the visit count and stamps with country flags
  • An RSS feed of updates in four languages and a “Follow the project” button
  • Preview cards for each section when you hover the menu
  • The “five pillars” hang on a string and flutter like a paper flag

Improved

  • The page under the cursor is loaded in advance, so navigation is almost instant
  • Buttons fill with colour like ink, and a second photo peeks out from behind the section cards
  • Wikimedia Commons photos are gradually moving onto the site itself: faster and more reliable

item.title: Site · v3.6 · A new look: a family photo album from 2011
item.description:
The site no longer looks like a tech template. It now feels like an album you leaf through at home: paper, white-bordered prints, handwritten captions and the orange date of a digital camera on the photos.

New

  • Alegreya for headings, Literata for text, handwritten Caveat for captions
  • Archive photos, Unreal frames and previews as taped prints
  • The author’s story is laid out as a letter instead of a dark slide
  • The dark theme is now an album under a lamp, without the cold blue

Improved

  • Project figures and milestones are written in the margins instead of grey tiles

item.title: Site · v3.5 · A Donetsk quiz: 53 photos, a city map and a photo of the day
item.description:
The small 14-photo guessing game is now a full quiz: 53 photos from 2008–2013 of 19 places in the city and four modes.

New

  • Where on the map?: put a pin on the map of Donetsk, points depend on the distance
  • Guess the year: taken before 2011, in 2011 or later
  • Photo of the day: one photo for everyone, one try and a result in squares for Telegram and Instagram
  • Shared stats: each photo shows how many players got it right
  • Readers’ photos: your own 2008–2012 shots can be sent by email, and the best go into the quiz and the archive

Improved

  • Guess the place: 19 places instead of 7, from the railway station and the airport to the slag heaps
  • A new map of the whole city from OpenStreetMap: roads, rivers, ponds, parks

item.title: Site · v3.4 · Before/after, a live preview and memories without GitHub
item.description:
The site shows more: blockout progress is visible with a slider, the home page plays a live model of the quarter, and a memory can now be sent as an ordinary email.

New

  • A before/after comparison on the Development page and in the updates feed
  • A live video of the 3D quarter on the home page that opens the model in one click
  • Memory map: sending by email without an account, fields for text and signature
  • Guess the place: after answering you can add a memory of that place straight away

Improved

  • The home video is 0.6 MB, loads only when visible and does not play with data saver or reduced motion
  • The Contact section on the Press page: the author’s email

item.title: Site · v3.3 · Press kit and faster loading
item.description:
The site got lighter and easier to share: moving between pages is several times faster and links now show proper previews.

New

  • A Press page: description, facts, images and a logo
  • Link previews for Telegram, Instagram and social networks on every page
  • A custom 404 page

Improved

  • Shared styles and scripts are cached: moving between pages loads 12–35 times less
  • 3D quarter data loads only on Reconstruction
  • A sitemap and structured data for search engines

item.title: Site · v3.1 · The update feed
item.description:
A new page gathers every change to the game, the site and the research into one feed.

New

  • Filter by game, site or research
  • “New” marks since your last visit and a counter in the menu
  • A stage rail: where the project is now
  • A link to every entry and a latest-update card on the home page

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The northern road and the gate from the 2011 panoramas
item.description:
The northern road and the house 33 gate were checked against the October 2011 panoramas: planting on the east verge, scalloped concrete panels, sheet metal turning to brick at label 27. DX11: 27 surface checks, 3 routes, 22 captures.

New

  • 7 trees, 10 shrubs and a low wall on the east verge
  • Scalloped concrete gate panels with relief joints
  • A low board fence north of label 30

Improved

  • A soft dirt-to-asphalt edge at the gate
  • Shrubs and a tree on the west verge

item.title: Site · v3.0 · The real Donetsk and a model of the quarter
item.description:
Grey captures gave way to photographs of the city from 2008–2013 and renders of the 3D model lit by the October 2011 sun.

New

  • A 22-photo archive with filters and a full-screen viewer
  • The 3D quarter with shadows and a sun slider set to 15 October 2011
  • A walk through the 3D model with Back and Next buttons
  • “Guess the place”: 14 photos, 7 places and a best score

Improved

  • A hero image of Donetsk at dusk in November 2011
  • Development in order: goal, method, engine, blockout, plan, log
  • Unreal captures gathered in the Blockout section

Fixed

  • Removed the link to the deleted atlas

item.title: Site · v2.1 · Comfortable on a phone
item.description:
The mobile version got a pinned menu and tidier typography.

New

  • The ☰ menu is pinned to the top of the screen

Improved

  • The log shows the last 4 entries on phones
  • Headings scale to fit the screen width

Fixed

  • Long words no longer break in the middle
  • Pages no longer slide sideways on narrow screens

item.title: Site · v2.0 · Four pages instead of one
item.description:
The site is split into Home, The city, Reconstruction and Development. Each page answers its own question.

New

  • A page menu and quick links to sections

Improved

  • The gist of the atlas moved into the memory map caption

Fixed

  • Removed repeated blocks

item.title: Game · AP-01 · Planting before the northern building
item.description: The October 2011 south view showed dense greenery on the west verge. The model now has four shrubs and a small tree there; the full DX11 run passed 27 checks and 3 routes.

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The north of the quarter and the first 67 metres
item.description:
The north of the quarter: a retaining wall with a lawn and conifers, end-wall windows and a service court without the misplaced annex. The first 67 m of the street got trees, shrubs, dirt shoulders and separate surfaces.

New

  • A retaining wall, a raised lawn and three conifers
  • Windows and projecting edges on the end facade
  • 7 trees, 7 shrubs and 4 garden clusters on the first segment

Improved

  • Asphalt, patches, dirt and gravel are now separate surfaces

Fixed

  • Removed a misplaced annex that blocked the service lane

item.title: Site · v1.4 · The memory map
item.description:
Anyone who remembers Donetsk can mark a place on the map and leave a memory.

New

  • A 4.37 × 2.84 km map of the centre where you pick a point
  • Submission through a GitHub form with the place's coordinates
  • The memory appears on the site after review

item.title: Site · v1.3 · The 3D quarter, a walk and a game
item.description:
The site became interactive: you can fly over the quarter, walk the street and remember the city in a game.

New

  • A 280 × 660 m 3D model of the quarter right in the browser
  • Evidence mode: every house shows what is known and what is estimated
  • A walk down Zarichna through 9 panorama points from 2011
  • The “Guess the place” game and the sound diary shelf

Improved

  • “New” marks in the development log

item.title: Game · AP-01 · An observation walk in the game
item.description:
The playable quarter now starts at house 33 and guides the player through six October 2011 panorama points. The HUD shows what is known and what is estimated.

New

  • Six steps through the 2011 panorama points
  • A restrained HUD without money or missions

Improved

  • The crowd walks only along the east verge of the quarter
  • A tool for repeatable drive-through captures

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The working quarter of Zarichna and Donetska
item.description:
A working Zarichna and Donetska quarter, 280 × 660 m: 189 volumes, SRTM terrain and a continuous 412 m corridor based on six October 2011 panoramas. 18 surface checks, ≈ 564 m routes along each street and 38 GIS tests passed.

New

  • 189 volumes from individual OSM outlines
  • SRTM terrain under the whole quarter
  • A continuous 412 m corridor from six panoramas

Improved

  • 18 surface checks and 38 GIS tests

item.title: Research · M01 · Checking OSM from 2012
item.description: OSM in 2012 compared with today's map: 91 candidates, 18 reviewed. None entered the 2011 canon without dated imagery.

item.title: Site · v1.2 · Why the city is out of reach
item.description:
The home page gained Davito Daveeni's 2012 film about Donetsk and figures with sources.

New

  • A section on why there is no way back to Donetsk
  • The 2012 documentary with thanks to its author

Improved

  • Every figure checked and sourced

item.title: Game · AP-01 · The first Windows player
item.description:
The first Windows player with a pause menu, saving and loading. A 54 m frontage study near no. 33 and eight frames captured straight from Unreal.

New

  • Pause menu, saving and loading
  • A 54 m facade study at house 33

item.title: Site · v1.0 · The site goes live
item.description:
Project website launched in four languages.

New

  • Russian, Ukrainian, English and Finnish
  • A personal story and Street View panoramas from 2011
  • A photo archive of Donetsk before 2014
  • A live Donetsk 2011 clock and a ticker of streets

item.title: Game · M02 · Moving to Unreal Engine 5.8
item.description: Move to Unreal Engine 5.8.3: the Development Editor build succeeded and the game launched on DX11. Decision DEC-0001: I start the First Playable while research continues in parallel.

item.title: Game · P0 · The Unity prototype
item.description: Unity prototype: 6 routes over 1,200 m, 1,002 ground samples, Windows and Android test builds.

item.title: Research · M01 · The October 2011 panoramas
item.description: October 2011 Street View panoramas walked along Zarichna Street in both directions. The audit of 126 footprints found no overlaps.

item.title: Research · M01 · The origin point
item.description: Origin confirmed: 33 Zarichna St, 47.9927461 N, 37.8183736 E.

item.title: Research · M01 · The reference map of the centre
item.description: OpenStreetMap snapshot: 8,508 elements, a 4.37 × 2.84 km reference map of the centre.
